title: Discourse inline-onebox titles can cause content-amplification denial of service
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not identified for this finding)
summary: An attacker-controlled or untrusted remote page can supply a very long title that Discourse processes and inserts through inline oneboxing. The primary project release note describes this as content-amplification denial of service; the fix bounds normalized titles to 500 characters before caching or insertion into cooked posts. The source does not specify an exact network-level exploit scenario beyond remote metadata and resource exhaustion.
ai_role: The official Discourse release changelog identifies the original security change (#45745, backported as #45747) as discovered by Anthropic OSS Scanner under finding ANT-2026-Y93QBLJB. Anthropic’s OSS Scanner documentation states fast-track reports come directly from its strongest models; no item-level model/version is given.
classification_note: The project’s primary security change labels this a content-amplification DoS and directly attributes discovery to Anthropic OSS Scanner. No CVE/GHSA was found in reviewed primary sources; use PR #45745 as the public issue identifier. No exploitation or zero-day claim is made.
remediation_note: The fix truncates normalized remote inline-onebox titles to 500 characters before caching or inserting into cooked posts. The change was backported to release 2026.9 (#45747), 2026.10 (#45749), and 2026.7 (#45748). Deployed patch status is not checked.
